<thought>The data indicate a molecule with formula C₁₆H₁₆O (m/z 224.1201, ~16 ¹³C atoms). The ¹³C NMR shows a carbonyl (~197 ppm), two aliphatic CH₂ carbons (~36–38 ppm), a methyl carbon (~26 ppm), and twelve aromatic carbons, consistent with two phenyl rings. The ¹H NMR integrates to 3 H (singlet, aromatic methyl), two triplets of 2 H each (–CH₂–CH₂–), and nine aromatic protons (7 H overlapping + 2 H), matching a para‑methyl phenyl ring (4 H) plus an unsubstituted phenyl ring (5 H). The structure that fits all these features is a ketone where one phenyl ring is directly attached to the carbonyl and the other phenyl ring (para‑methyl) is linked via a –CH₂–CH₂– chain. The SMILES for this structure is:

O=C(c1ccccc1)CCc2ccc(cc2)C

This SMILES yields C₁₆H₁₆O and reproduces the observed spectral pattern.
